data.description:
Welcome to Seeking Alpha's Catalyst Watch - a breakdown of some of next week's actionable events that stand out. Read more about the events that may impact stock prices next week.

 

Monday - October 5

  • Volatility watch - Astera Labs (ALAB) and Lumentum (LITE) have seen options volatility increase over the last week. The most overbought stocks per their 14-day Relative Strength Index include Armada Acquisition Corp. II (XRPN), Kodiak Sciences (KOD), and Pacific Bio (PACB). The most oversold stocks per their 14-day Relative Strength Index include Advasa Holdings (ADBT) and MGM Resorts (MGM). Short interest is elevated on TeraWulf (WULF) and C4 Therapeutics (CCCC).
  • Dividend watch - Companies that have an ex-dividend date coming next week include GE Aerospace (GE), Comcast (CMCSA), AT&T (T), and Verizon (VZ).
  • All day - Dillard's (DDS), Energy Transfer (ET), Sunoco (SUN), and Texas Capital Bancshares (TCBI) are some of the notable companies that will start trading on the Texas Stock Exchange as their primary listings.
  • All day - It is the first trading day after the OPEC+ production policy meeting on October 4.
  • All day - The two-day Energy Intelligence Forum 2026 will begin. The event is designed to bring together energy executives, investors, policymakers, analysts, and civil-society leaders to debate how the energy system can remain secure and affordable while decarbonizing. Notable speakers include Aramco (ARMCO) CEO Amin Nasser, Eni (E) CEO Claudio Descalzi, BP (BP) CEO Meg O’Neill, and Total Energies (TTE) CEO Patrick Pouyanné.

 

Tuesday - October 6

  • Earnings watch - Notable companies due to report include Constellation Brands (STZ), Lamb Weston (LW), and RPM International (RPM).
  • Sales events - Amazon (AMZN) will hold its two-day Prime Big Deal Days, with deals for Prime members. Target’s competing Target Circle Deal Days also runs October 6–7, with offers for members of its free loyalty program. Walmart's (WMT) weeklong Fall Deals sale runs October 5–11, and it does not require a membership.
  • All day - Notable investor events include Zscaler's (ZS) Investor Day and Nomad Foods' (NOMD) Investor Day. The tech sector will have its eyes on Marvell Technology's (MRVL) Investor Day, which will feature CEO Matt Murphy and other executives discussing the company’s strategy, growth opportunities, and role in next-generation AI and data-center infrastructure.
  • All day - The three-day NACS Show will begin. The annual convenience-store and fuel-retailing conference will include participation from Casey's General Stores (CASY), Accenture (ACN), Dollar General (DG), 7-Eleven, QuikTrip, Love's, Circle K, and Sunoco (SUN).
  • All day - Executives with NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), Palo Alto Networks (PANW), and Booz Allen Hamilton (BAH) will give speeches at the ICS Cybersecurity Conference.
  • All day - The mega media merger between Paramount Skydance (PSKY) and Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) is expected to close. Skydance will be the name of the combined company and the new ticker will be SKYD.

 

Wednesday - October 7

  • Earnings watch - Notable companies due to report include Levi Strauss (LEVI) and Applied Digital (APLD).
  • All day - Neogen (NEOG) will hold an Investor Day event. The focus of the event will be on Neogen's strategic transformation as the company provides additional details on its commercial prowess, high-impact innovation, and operational drive toward sustainable improvement in financial performance.
  • 1:00 p.m. Microsoft (MSFT) will hold its Windows and Surface event. The event is expected to focus on local AI in Windows and Surface devices, with possible updates on the Surface Laptop Ultra, Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, and Windows 11. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Windows and Surface chief Pavan Davuluri, and Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang are expected to attend.
  • 2:00 p.m. The Federal Reserve will release the minutes from its last meeting.
  • Postmarket - Costco (COST) monthly sales report.

 

Thursday - October 8

  • Earnings watch - Notable companies due to report include PepsiCo (PEP) and Tilray Brands (TLRY).
  • All day - The IPO lockup period expires on certain blocks of shares of SK hynix (SKHY).
  • All day - Notable investor events include Mission Produce's (AVO) Investor Day.
  • All day - Circana will release videogame sales results for August.
  • All day - Zeta Global (ZETA) will hold its Zeta Live event. Speakers include Zeta CEO David Steinberg, ZoomInfo (GTM) CEO Henry Schuck, and Taboola (TBLA) CEO Adam Singolda.
  • All day - Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem speaks at a Bloomberg Event on the U.S. economy and policy.
  • 8:15 a.m. PepsiCo (PEP) will hold its earnings conference call. Investors will be focused on whether PepsiCo can sustain its early North American volume recovery, while protecting margins amid heavier brand investment, and affordability initiatives. Some analysts think the food and beverage giant's prior full-year outlook is at risk of a downward revision. Celsius Holdings (CELH) derives more than 40% of its revenue from PepsiCo and traded in tandem with it on earnings day 88% of the time.

 

Friday - October 9

  • Earnings watch - Notable companies due to report include Delta Air Lines (DAL).
  • 4:00 p.m. - Nasdaq will release its latest update on short positions on stocks.

 

Seeking Alpha Editor Joshua Fineman contributed to this article.

data.title: BNY in talks with Kraken parent for digital asset infrastructure pact - report
data.description:
BNY (BNY), the custody bank powerhouse, has entered talks with Payward, the parent of crypto exchange Kraken (KRAKEN), to form a broad partnership encompassing digital assets and financial market infrastructure, according to a media report on Friday.

The potential partnership may offer crypto products, custody, wealth management, trading, payments, and infrastructure, CoinDesk reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. Talks are ongoing, and there's no guarantee that a deal will be reached.

Parts of the proposed agreement could be similar to the infrastructure component of Payward's recent partnership with Nasdaq, one of the people told CoinDesk.

An agreement would advance Payward's progress to connect its digital-asset operations with established financial institutions. From a broader perspective, it would underscore the inroads that digital assets are continuing to make into more traditional financial systems.

BNY (BNY) stock rose 1.3% in Friday afternoon trading.

Last month, Nasdaq (NDAQ) agreed to invest $100M  in Payward as they expand their partnership to develop infrastructure for tokenized markets. Kraken is set to distribute Nasdaq's tokenized stocks on its platform, giving investors access to Nasdaq-listed stocks in tokenized form.

data.title: AI boom shields stocks from G7 bond bear market: Jefferies
data.description:
A sharp decline in U.S. consumer confidence signals an impending political rout for Republicans in the upcoming midterm elections, even as surging AI-driven corporate earnings continue to insulate equities (SPY) (QQQ) (DIA) from a severe sell-off in sovereign bond markets, according to Jefferies.

The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index dropped to the lowest level since April 2014 in September, prompting analyst Christopher Wood to "assume, until proven otherwise, that a rout is facing the Republicans in the forthcoming mid-term elections." The economic strain is evident in housing markets, where mortgage rates have climbed to 7.3%, a multi-year high, driving mortgage applications down 37% year-over-year.

Prediction market traders on Kalshi estimate a 63% probability that the Democratic Party will win control of the U.S. Senate in the midterms, compared with a 37% chance for the Republican Party. The GOP had higher odds of winning up until mid-September.

Despite political headwinds, U.S. equities have remained resilient. S&P 500 third-quarter 2026 earnings are expected to rise 30.2% from a year ago, driven by a 65.1% earnings surge in the Information Technology sector (XLK) and 131.7% growth in semiconductors (SMH) (SOXX). This strong performance, fueled by the highly earnings-accretive AI capex cycle, has allowed stocks to largely shrug off rising bond yields (US2Y) (US10Y) (US30Y) and geopolitical tensions, Wood said.

The bond market, however, tells a different story. Ten-year (IEF) and 30-year Treasury (ZROZ) yields this week reached their highest levels since 2002. Wood maintains his thesis that G7 government bonds have entered a "structural bear market" following a 39-year bull run, with the 10-year yield rising 82 basis points last quarter alone.

The bond rout has triggered tremors across credit markets. The MOVE index, which measures Treasury bond market volatility, has spiked to levels last seen during the U.S.-Israel attack on Iran, while high-yield corporate spreads have begun widening. Wood warned that "the real damage in the credit space cannot be seen on a mark-to-market basis. That, of course, is private credit (VPC) (HYIN)."

Meanwhile, emerging market local-currency government bonds (EMB) have continued to outperform their G7 counterparts, beating the Bloomberg G7 government bond index by 59% in U.S. dollar terms since March 2020—a trend Wood expects to persist.

Dear readers: We recognize that politics often intersects with the financial news of the day, so we invite you to click here to join the separate political discussion.

SA Asks: Is IBM a buy, hold or sell right now? (Update)
data.description:
Shares of IBM (IBM) are still down 25% year-to-date after the stock plunged in mid-July on disappointing preliminary Q2 earnings results.  

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Bashar Issa, Mike Zaccardi, and Dhierin Bechai whether they thought Big Blue was a buy, hold, or sell right now. 

Bashar Issa: I rate IBM (IBM) a Hold. Few companies have disappointed me as much as IBM because I know it can do better. They have unparalleled access via go-to mainframes and servers, complemented by an extensive software portfolio. Yet, over the past decade, they've managed to miss almost every major secular tailwind that came their way, from Public Cloud migration to AI infrastructure buildout.  

Enterprise AI is a new opportunity. We'll have to wait and see whether IBM can capitalize on this to generate growth. 

Mike Zaccardi: IBM is a Buy right now. Yes, there are headwinds related to the company's recently lowered fiscal year revenue outlook, along with an admittedly messy technical situation, but Big Blue remains a decent value play in an industry that can see rapid re-ratings. Its free cash flow per share is $14.02 over the past 12 months. That's a better-than 6% FCF yield, while the dividend yield has popped above 3% (almost two percentage points above the S&P 500's).  

I see the stock as materially de-risked heading into the Q3 print, but watch out for a big move after it reports on October 21. The options market prices in a large 7.1% post-earnings stock price swing. 

Dhierin Bechai: I believe shares of IBM (IBM) are a Buy. The company is not high growth, but the stock price decline served as a much-needed reset and actually overshot on that correction. 

The risk is that IBM may continue losing out in the CapEx allocation puzzle, but underlying mainframe demand still remains strong. It is not the case that AI is permanently replacing mainframes. IBM is just losing out for now in the CapEx allocation, but refreshes of critical on-premise hardware and connected licenses cannot be deferred indefinitely.

(Dhierin Bechai leads the SA investing group The Aerospace Forum.)

data.title: Blue Owl maintains 5% tender cap on two BDCs amid elevated withdrawal requests
data.description:
Two of Blue Owl Capital Inc.'s (OWL) private credit funds told shareholders that redemption requests have eased from Q1 2026's peak, though they remain well above the funds' 5% tender cap.

In letters to shareholders, Blue Owl Credit Income Corp., or OCIC, and Blue Owl Technology Income Corp., or OTIC, said credit quality for both funds remained resilient during the quarter.

Earlier this year, fears over AI's potential to eat into established software businesses sparked a rush of redemption requests across private credit firms, many of which are heavily weighted to investments in software companies.

Private business development companies, or BDCs, known for directly lending to mid-market businesses, allow investors to request share redemptions for limited periods of time.

For its Q3 window, OTIC received repurchase requests for $1.1B, or 39.0% of shares outstanding as of June 30, 2026, stable with the previous quarter's $1.1B, or 38.1%, and down from $1.2B, or 40.4%, in Q1 when demand peaked, the fund said. The fund will fulfill ~13% of total shares tendered.

Meanwhile, OTIC said its non-accruals stood at 0.3% of fair value. Its average annual gain of $0.06 for every $100 invested since inception has outperformed a senior secured middle market loan index's average net loss of $0.38 in the closest comparable period, the letter said.

"These results underscore the disconnect between the market’s fears of AI disintermediating software and OTIC’s resilient credit fundamentals," the fund said.

For OCIC, tender demand was $3.1B, or 16.8% of shares outstanding as of June 30, 2026, compared with $3.6B, or 18.8%, in Q2 and $4.2B, or 21.9%, in Q1. "We believe this continued improvement was supported by OCIC’s strong year-to-date performance and resilient portfolio fundamentals amid this year’s market volatility," the fund said.

OCIC will fulfill ~30% of total shares tendered.

As of midyear, OCIC's non-accruals were 0.2% of fair value and an average annual net loss of $0.15 for every $100 invested since inception. That compares with a senior secured middle market loan index net credit loss of $0.27 over the closest comparable period.

Both funds said they're well positioned to fulfill tender offers without selling private loans. As of Aug. 31, 2026, OTIC had $1.2B in available liquidity relative to the $135M Q3 tender offer. OCIC had $11.2B of available liquidity as compared with the $0.9B Q3 tender offer.

The funds also touted their longer-term returns. Since inception in May 2022, OTIC generated a 9.0% annualized total return for Class I shareholders. Meanwhile, since OCIC's start in March 2021, the fund generated a 9.2% annualized total return for class I shareholders, "meaningfully outperforming public credit indices," it said.

Blue Owl (OWL) stock rose 2.5% in Friday afternoon trading. Year to date, OWL shares have dropped 40%.

data.title: Mortgage sector: Navigating rising rates, credit cycle risks
data.description:
Investors Should Know: Mortgage insurance and residential mortgage finance companies are navigating one of the most challenging rate environments in years. Treasury yields and mortgage rates are near multiyear highs, squeezing affordability, suppressing origination volumes, and accelerating credit-loss normalization.

However, the pressure is not uniform across the sector. Mortgage insurers, originators, and mortgage REITs each face a distinct set of risks and potential offsets.

Key Takeaways

  • Rising Treasury yields are transmitting directly into mortgage rates, pushing the 30-year fixed rate to a three-year high and driving both purchase and refinance application volumes sharply lower.
  • Mortgage insurers benefit from portfolio persistency when refinancing is low, but aging delinquencies and rising loss provisions are emerging as the more important forward risk.
  • Mortgage originators face weak transaction volumes industry-wide, but scale, servicing income, and market-share gains can partially offset the headwinds for larger platforms.
  • Mortgage REITs carry higher asset yields in this environment due to agency MBS, but funding costs, leverage, and book-value volatility remain significant offsetting risks.
  • Analyst coverage is broadly split. Bulls point to persistency, servicing income, and eventual rate normalization as structural supports. At the same time, bears flag prolonged affordability pressure and credit-cycle normalization as the key constraints.

Background: How Rising Rates Are Reshaping Mortgage Sector Dynamics

The mortgage sector encompasses companies that insure residential loans against borrower default, originate and service home loans, and hold mortgage-backed securities as investments. Each business model has a different relationship with interest rates, credit performance, and housing transaction volumes.

When mortgage rates rise sharply, housing affordability deteriorates, fewer buyers can qualify for loans, and homeowners with low existing rates have little incentive to refinance. That dynamic reduces the flow of new business across the sector. For mortgage insurers specifically, however, lower refinancing activity also means fewer existing insured loans are paid off early, which can support the size and durability of the existing insured portfolio.

The credit cycle adds a second layer of complexity. Periods of low mortgage rates and strong home-price appreciation tend to keep delinquency low, as borrowers can refinance out of difficulty or sell at a gain. As rates rise and affordability weakens, delayed delinquencies and loss provisions can begin to increase, even when the overall default rate remains historically modest.

Stocks to Watch: MTG, ESNT, NMIH, RDN, RKT

MGIC Investment Corporation (MTG) and Essent Group Ltd. (ESNT) are the two most extensively covered private mortgage insurers in recent SA analysis, with NMI Holdings (NMIH) and Radian Group (RDN) also representing the core private mortgage insurance peer group. Rocket Companies (RKT) operates as a large-scale mortgage originator and servicer rather than a mortgage insurer, giving it a different earnings profile tied more directly to origination volumes and servicing portfolio size.

On the mortgage REIT side, names with exposure to agency mortgage-backed securities and residential whole loans include AGNC Investment Corp. (AGNC), Rithm Capital Corp. (RITM), and Ladder Capital Corp. (LADR). The VanEck Mortgage REIT Income ETF (MORT) provides broad exposure to the mortgage REIT category as a whole.

News Roundup

  • The 10-year Treasury yield moved above 5.25% and the 30-year exceeded 5.57%, with Lawrence Yun of the National Association of Realtors and Ali Wolf of Zonda both describing housing conditions as slow and challenging as higher bond yields flowed into mortgage rates.
  • The 30-year fixed mortgage rate reached a three-year high of 7.28%, with the 15-year rate at 6.60%; Mortgage Bankers Association CEO Bob Broeksmit said affordability and borrower demand had weakened materially.
  • Mortgage applications declined 6.0% in the most recent week covered, with purchase applications down 4.3% and refinance applications falling 8.7%; MBA economist Joel Kan said activity had reached its slowest weekly pace since 2025.
  • Mortgage insurance stocks sold off broadly, with MGIC, NMI Holdings, Essent Group, and Radian Group all retreating as investors reacted to sector-wide concerns about credit-cycle risk and loss normalization.
  • KB Home management reported lower housing revenue and acknowledged pressure from higher rates, pricing, and resale competition; Executive Chairman Jeffrey Mezger said a modest improvement in consumer confidence could lift demand.
  • Wells Fargo renewed its mortgage loan servicing system agreement with Intercontinental Exchange, signaling continued investment in servicing infrastructure across the industry.

What Analysts Say

SA contributor analysis on the mortgage sector reflects a consistent tension: near-term operating metrics remain relatively solid for the larger mortgage insurers and for Rocket's servicing platform, but the forward risk profile is deteriorating as the credit cycle turns and affordability remains constrained. Coverage of mortgage REITs is similarly split between income potential and structural volatility risks.

Bulls across the sector point to portfolio persistency, servicing income durability, and the eventual benefit of rate normalization. Bears focus on aging delinquencies, rising loss provisions, and the difficulty of expanding valuation multiples while credit losses are still moving higher.

Analyst Commentary

Growth Stock Hunter: MGIC Investment (MTG) — views MGIC as fundamentally the strongest mortgage insurer in the covered peer group based on reported ROE and book-value growth, but argues that rising delinquencies, credit-loss normalization, and the mechanics of reinsurance arrangements limit the degree to which that fundamental strength can translate into multiple expansion from current levels. Read more.

Growth Stock Hunter: Essent Group (ESNT) — describes Essent's core mortgage insurance business as stable, supported by a 13.4% ROAE, but flags the increase in the mortgage-insurance loss ratio to 13.6% and rising provision reserves as evidence that the credit cycle is moving against the company, with uncertainty around Essent's expansion into property-and-casualty reinsurance adding an additional layer of risk to the valuation outlook. Read more.

Nicolas Bolsinger: Rocket Companies (RKT) — frames Rocket as a cycle-recovery opportunity, arguing that record market share, direct-to-consumer rate-lock volume growth from $28.4 billion to $36.9 billion, and a large servicing portfolio make the current period a potential entry point for a company whose valuation appears to reflect trough conditions rather than a normalized earnings environment. Read more.

Rida Morwa: Mortgage REITs — argues that the current rate environment has improved reinvestment economics for agency MBS holders, as higher yields on newly originated mortgages make the asset class more attractive, though emphasizes that total returns remain highly dependent on the trajectory of interest rates and the spread between asset yields and hedged funding costs. Read more.

On the Pulse: VanEck Mortgage REIT Income ETF (MORT) — highlights the income potential of broad mortgage REIT exposure at current distribution yields, noting that AGNC's tangible book value increased 2.4% in the most recent quarter discussed and that Rithm benefited from its broader origination, servicing, and asset-management platform, while cautioning that equity, leverage, and book-value volatility risks are material. Read more.

Albert Anthony: Ladder Capital (LADR) — identifies Ladder as a diversified mortgage REIT trading below book value with investment-grade ratings and a relatively modest leverage profile versus peers, but flags declining operating margins, earnings compression, and office-loan exposure as risks that justify the discount. Read more.
